persona: Impatient first-time hobbyist aiming for a short cinematic cue

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Instrument creation, drawing notes, naming, and exports were discoverable. Cutting and deleting selected clip pieces took an undo and a separate selection step; playback recovery did not succeed.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark teal arrangement, readable waveform shapes, and clean piano roll feel polished. Similar clip colors and subtle selection outlines made destructive selection behavior less obvious.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most editing actions responded promptly and repeating material was quick. WAV export took roughly 30 seconds for a 30-second cue, and playback failure interrupted the workflow. This reflects the laboratory session, not a hardware benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Tool help resolved duplication quickly, and held-drag duration feedback was clear. Erase acted on both selected split pieces, and Play eventually did nothing visibly after Audio setup recovery.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The visible tools covered the requested audio arrangement, MIDI editing, real VST instrument assignment, project save, WAV export, and MIDI export. Broader production features and other plug-ins were not evaluated.

findings.title: Empty-track instruction leads directly to instrument assignment
findings.observation: Double-clicking the area labeled Double-click for MIDI opened the device library. Choosing Assign instrument created a MIDI track and pattern labeled with Rill Lab Sine.

findings.title: Drawing beyond the initial MIDI clip extends it
findings.observation: Pencil drags created a C4, D-sharp4, G4, G-sharp4, G4 phrase, and the clip end moved from one bar to almost four bars without a separate resize operation.

findings.title: Duplicate is a persistent tool rather than a one-click command
findings.observation: Selecting Duplicate alone did not create a clip. Tool help explicitly said to click a clip; that made the next action clear.

findings.title: Erasing after a split removed both selected pieces
findings.observation: Cutting the final audio repetition at 30 seconds and then clicking its right piece with Erase removed the entire repetition, shortening the arrangement to 25.714 seconds. Undo restored the pieces. Clearing selection and selecting only the right piece before Erase produced 30.000 seconds.

findings.title: Held-drag readout makes exact lengths achievable
findings.observation: The MIDI resize tooltip showed seconds and beats. After one overshoot to 8.705 seconds, another small drag reached 8.571 seconds and 16 beats. The final repeated MIDI clip was trimmed to End 30.000 seconds and Duration 8 beats.

findings.title: Mouse-only naming and save were supported visibly
findings.observation: Rename project exposed a Keyboard button and on-screen keys. Entering ember rise populated the native project-save filename, already pointed at session-4.

findings.title: Playback output failed and ordinary recovery did not restore visible transport movement
findings.observation: The first Play showed active meters for both Circuit drums and New instrument. The next screenshot showed a moved playhead near bar 1 beat 4 and Audio output stream failed or disconnected. A later Play attempt immediately showed the same warning. Audio setup, Refresh devices, and Apply cleared the warning, but repeated Play clicks showed no transport movement. Mixer navigation still responded.

findings.title: Both exports succeeded, but WAV required waiting
findings.observation: Export WAV correctly described Arrangement 0:30; effect tails were unchecked. The native picker supplied ember rise.wav. Export was still running at 14 seconds, and menu clicks during it had no visible effect. A later screenshot showed Exported ember rise.wav. Export MIDI supplied ember rise.mid and showed success almost immediately.

outcome.status: Project saved and both exports visibly completed; playback remained unresolved
outcome.composition: At 112 BPM, fourteen bars of starter Circuit rhythm audio accompany a repeated ascending minor-flavored C4/D-sharp4/G4/G-sharp4/G4 sine phrase. Four repetitions were created; the last audio and MIDI clips were shortened to two bars.
outcome.instrument: Rill Lab Sine, visible VST3 library entry and MIDI-track assignment
outcome.independent_artifact_verification: Pending coordinator verification; this participant did not inspect app data or exported file contents.

limitations: Simulated usability research, not a human participant study.
Used only the provided visible mouse driver and screenshots for the application; no keyboard events, source reads, state APIs, composition-file edits, or peer records.
No audio capture was auditioned. Meter activity and transport movement do not establish audible quality.
Playback encountered an output-stream failure in the timer-paced virtual audio environment; the cause was not determined.
The application showed 30.000 seconds and successful exports, but exact exported duration, PCM, MIDI contents, and instrument render must be checked independently.
Only the installed Rill Lab Sine VST3 instrument was used; no general claim about third-party plug-ins or physical device latency is made.
The cue used the supplied startup audio and a newly drawn MIDI phrase; no external audio was imported.
